reason: The cited evidence (E2, E4, E5) directly supports the electronic interaction, anionic shell, and stability of POM-protected gold nanoparticles under heating and base addition in non-polar solvents. However, all evidence is limited to monometallic gold nanoparticles, and no passage addresses multi-metal high-entropy alloys or the extreme temperature range up to 1923 K, leaving the generalization premise unsupported.
premises: Multi-dentate POM ligands form a robust electronic interaction with metal nanoparticles
This interaction creates an anionic POM layer that prevents agglomeration
The POM-protected nanoparticles remain stable under heating (up to 90 °C) and in the presence of bases
The method works in non-polar solvents like toluene
The cited evidence on gold nanoparticles generalizes to nanoparticles of five or more metals in equal ratios
